issues.title: Regress: G1 walking flagship (v067 whole-body kernel) cannot keep standing prior upright past 250/720 steps
issues.description:
The cmaesEngine.test.ts test "the shipped owner package executes every CMA family plus both robot flagships" expects the standing-only prior to survive >336 steps and the curriculum to complete 720 steps. With the v067 (whole-body, 30-link) kernel, the standing prior fails at step 250 ("base height") and the curriculum fails at step 283 ("base height") — both before the 264-step push-pulse start. v066 (16-link) passed at 512 steps ("base tilt" after the pulse). The v067 addition of arms/head/upper-body as kernel-posed dynamic bodies has destabilized the prior/curriculum.

User directive (priority): the robot must walk AS FAR AS POSSIBLE, AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE, AND AS STABLY AS POSSIBLE, with a MULTI-FACTOR OBJECTIVE OVER TIME. The current single-scalar rollup weights actuator work and slip too aggressively; it punishes a stabilizing prior that is doing small corrective work, so the prior falls early. The new objective should integrate per-step signals over the trajectory and expose (a) distance / time -> mean forward speed, (b) cumulative stability (tilt, slip, contact, impact) over time, and (c) survival duration, all without reward-hacking collapse.

Acceptance criteria:
- v067 G1 standing prior survives the disclosed pulse (steps 264–336) on the standard terrain-and-push config; target: completedSteps > 336 in the existing test.
- v67 G1 walking curriculum completes the full 720 steps (horizon) on the same config.
- v67 G1 5,040-D optimization still improves the curriculum baseline across multiple declared seeds without reward hacking.
- New multi-factor objective over time: the receipt exposes both per-step and trajectory-aggregated versions of (distance, speed vs target, stability — tilt/slip/contact/impact, work, push impulse, recovery, contact-schedule mismatch). The per-step signals drive a CMA-visible mean+penalty term so the optimizer cannot game a single rollup.
- Standing-prior baseline (no learning) achieves >1.0 m forward distance and >0.5 m/s mean forward speed over the 1.5 s horizon on the standard config.
- Curriculum mean (no learning) achieves >1.0 m forward distance and >0.5 m/s mean forward speed over the 1.5 s horizon.
- Optimized policy (5,040-D, default seed) improves over curriculum on the multi-factor objective across all three declared Philox seeds, with no per-seed cherry-picking.
- bun test passes the existing schema-7 G1 packet-adapter tests AND the end-to-end flagship test.
- typecheck, lint, build pass; desktop + mobile smoke passes with zero console/page/network errors.

Scope: kernel patch lives in /Users/jemanuel/projects/frankensim; this repo tracks the new artifacts and tests. Possible: new schema-8 (v068) for the per-step multi-factor signal.

issues.title: Training crate: PPO + GAE loop over parallel native rollouts
issues.description: PPO (clip 0.2) with GAE(lambda) over the bd-train-env-trait stepwise env, rayon-parallel across N envs (4k default), value head on the transformer (separate linear), entropy bonus, observation normalization running stats. 64-step horizons. Gates from RESEARCH_G1_LEARNING.md section 3.4: beats the linear residual policy on the identical terrain-and-push experiment within equal wall-clock, WITHOUT the phase basis.

issues.title: Training crate: Muon (Newton-Schulz) + Adam optimizers
issues.description: Muon for 2-D hidden weights: momentum buffer + Newton-Schulz orthogonalization (the 5-iteration quintic polynomial from Keller Jordan's reference), LR scaled 0.2x on the output head per the Muon literature. Adam(2e-4) for embed/head/norm params. Split config: param-name pattern -> optimizer. Unit tests: orthogonalization orthonormalizes (SVD check on small matrices), update math vs hand-computed values, LR split routing. Ref: arXiv 2509.24406.

issues.title: Training crate: tiny transformer policy (GLM-shrunk, ~4M params)
issues.description: Dense pre-norm decoder: 4 layers, d_model 256, 8 heads, GQA 4 kv heads, RoPE over the 64-step context, SwiGLU hidden 682, RMSNorm; input embed from 42 proprioception signals; linear head -> 29 targets. ~3-6M params (sizing math in RESEARCH_G1_LEARNING.md section 3.2). Rust: hand-rolled forward + reverse-mode grad (tensor ops in fs-la style, f64/f32) OR candle backend — decide by benchmark. Determinism law: seeded init (splitmix64), no wall clock. Unit tests: RoPE positions, GQA shapes, SwiGLU math, gradcheck (finite differences) on every param block.

issues.title: Training crate: stepwise G1 env API (reset/step) in native Rust
issues.description: Expose the 720-step rollout loop in fs-cmaes-viz-wasm/src/g1_walking.rs as a stepwise env: G1TrainEnv::reset(seed) -> Observation, step(action) -> (obs, reward_shaping, done, info). The rollout loop already evaluates G1ResidualPolicy per step (g1_walking.rs:659) — refactor into a pub stepwise API behind a feature flag so CMA-ES batch evaluate() stays untouched. Native build only (no wasm32). Dense per-step reward = the objective shaping terms decomposed to steps (fall guard -> -large at fall step, upright potential, forward progress delta, energy integral per step) — requires decomposing the final receipt objective into per-step parts in the same crate. This is the PPO/transformer substrate.

issues.title: Ablation section: phase-basis prior vs learned-from-scratch
issues.description: Main page + /humanoid section: both traces replayed on the same terrain-and-push experiment side by side — linear residual policy (Lie-informed phase basis, CMA-ES) vs learned-from-scratch transformer (PPO+Muon, CMA-ES HPO). Receipts side by side: objective, completedSteps, distance, energy. Honest framing: sample-efficiency vs ceiling; neither is 'the winner' — the tradeoff IS the lesson.

issues.title: Export trained policy: ONNX + browser inference badge in the G1 flagship
issues.description: Export the trained transformer to ONNX; serve from public/robots/g1/ (mirroring the mesh/kernel honesty pattern: metadata JSON with obs layout, action scaling, limits). G1 worker gains a third policy source: transformer (GPU-trained) via onnxruntime-web, badge 'policy: transformer (GPU-trained)' next to 'walking curriculum mean' / 'LM-CMA (live)'. Kernel refusal/schema envelope unchanged — WASM kernel still validates every rollout.

issues.title: Training crate: CMA-ES outer hyperparameter loop
issues.description: Reuse fs-dfo CMA-ES (pop 10) over 8-12 hyperparameters: inner LR (Muon/Adam), Muon momentum, entropy coefficient, reward weight vector (upright/contact/energy), GAE lambda, value coef. Each fitness evaluation = one full inner training run (truncated). This is where CMA-ES is genuinely strongest (small-D expensive black-box) — the demotion from weight-space to HPO-space per RESEARCH_G1_LEARNING.md section 3.3.

issues.title: Kernel: G1 house-navigation challenge variant
issues.description: New G1Challenge variant: HouseNavigation — start in the entry room, goal waypoint chain through doorways (waypoint gates in the objective: reach room k within time k). Requires bd-multi-obstacle-kernel (wall/furniture collision in rollout). The existing recovery/terrain machinery composes. Owner: frankensim (sibling crate, bead cmaes-nxj lineage).
